general_information.Description: Based on the study results of English language and specialized subjects in the previous semesters, students shall complete a Graduation thesis with the content and format appropriate to the research area to meet all course requirements. Thus, students are equipped with the knowledge and skills in scientific research and are able to present a research paper in English. For each student, the Graduation thesis is the capstone project of their undergraduate program. Through the Graduation thesis, students are equipped with the skills of finding a topic and persistently surveying, researching, and pursuing that topic, as well as practicing writing skills to present their arguments in a logical way. Thus, they can pursue self-learning even after graduation and nurture the capability for expressing their own thoughts and ideas. The Graduation thesis is conducted in GROUPS including 04 students (in case the students cannot be divided evenly, there can be a group of 3 or 5 students) The instruction on the Graduation thesis is organized in two ways: in-class and in separate groups. The in-class instruction is conducted in the first week with the content regarding the rules, regulations, and things to be noticed during the process of writing the Graduation thesis. From week 2 onwards, the groups shall meet with the Thesis supervisor separately to discuss more in-depth about the group's topic. The discussion with the Thesis supervisor can take place in many different forms appropriate to the availability of the supervisor and the students (meeting in class, online discussion, and email etc.). Thesis topic: the students can choose their topic in one of the following directions: (1) Specialized English (2) English in IT (3) English in Economics and Trade (4) Issues in applied linguistics (5) Issues in English language teaching and learning
general_information.StudentTasks: # Form groups, select and decide on a topic # Plan and divide the workload between the members of the group # Report the work completed on Google Form shared with group members and teacher # Attend all in-class sessions and private group meetings with the supervisor # Conduct, survey, and write the thesis based on the requirements of the thesis and the instructions of the supervisor # Submit the reports, thesis, and presentation slides by the deadline # Defend the thesis before a Graduation Thesis Council Students are required to attend at least 80% of scheduled meetings with their supervisor(s) to be eligible for the thesis or capstone defense.
general_information.Tools: # Search engines & online databases (e.g. Google Scholar; Semantic Scholar; ResearchGate, etc.) # Specific research-oriented AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT Deep Research; NotebookLM; Research Rabbit; SciSpace, etc.) # Writing and grammar check tools (e.g. Grammarly; Quillbot, etc.) # Data collection and analysis tools (Google Forms, SPSS, Excel, etc.) # Plagiarism checkers (e.g. Turnitin) # Reference Managers (e.g. Zotero; Mendeley, etc.) # APA Style Guide (https://apastyle.apa.org/style-grammar-guidelines/references/examples)
general_information.Note: A) Total: 100% 1. On-going Assessment: 60% 1.1. Report No.1: Research Proposal 5% 1.2. Report No.2: Literature Review 10% 1.3. Report No.3: Methodology 10% 1.4. Report No.4: Results / Finding 10% 1.5. Report No.5: Discussion, Conclusion, Limitations and Recommendations 10% 1.6. Report No.6: References 5% 1.7. Mock Thesis Defense: Presentation and Q&A: 10% 2. Final Assessment: 40% 2.1. Complete Written Report 15% 2.2. Oral Defense 25% A bonus mark for any thesis with research and application results can be added into both final assessments: Complete Written Report and Oral Defense (Oral Thesis Evaluation), as set out in the University Guidelines and Graduation Thesis Council Meeting Minutes. B) Completion Criteria: 2.1. Every on-going assessment component >0 2.2. Oral Defense >=5/10 2.3. Final Assessment (Complete Written Report + Oral Defense) >=5/10, each component >=5 2.4. Overall Result >=5/10

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Demonstrate knowledge of, and ability to select, appropriate research methods for an undergraduate-level thesis.
Apply a range of digital technology tools to facilitate research processes and enhance writing quality effectively, critically, and responsibly.
Adhere to key principles of reseach ethics, such as beneficience, integrity, and respect of intellectual property, at every stage of the research process.
Present scientific research procedures, findings, and analyses clearly, rigorously, and fluently in both written and verbal formats.
Develop autonomy and accountability in completing individual tasks and meeting research deadlines.
Demonstrate strong interpersonal communication and effective collaborative working skills.
Reference source materials thoroughly and accurately, and formatted to relevant international standards.
